title: One climb and out: 900m D+, fuelling test carrying it
terrain: alpine, ONE sustained climb ~900m D+, descent hard-capped 600m, lift-assisted down if available

steps.target: Z2-Z3 single sustained climb ~900m D+, 151-160 bpm
Z1-Z2 descent, capped 600m, poles, cadence 175+, 99-144 bpm

coachNotes:
EXECUTION: one climb and out. ~900m D+, descent hard-capped at 600m, take the lift down if there is one. Fixed line, fixed endpoint, load the GPX, no summit out-and-backs. Descend with poles, short stride, cadence 175+.
GYM: none.
FUEL, THE POINT OF THE DAY: 80 g/h held from minute 30 to the finish, measured. Race system is 1 Enervit Isocarb C2:1 Pro sachet (65g) per 500ml bottle per hour, 60g carbs and 600mg sodium, plus 1 Carbo Gel every second hour. If the Isocarb has not arrived, run on 2 Carbo Gels an hour with 200ml water each, and order it before 12 Sep. Write down grams per hour and what the stomach did at hour 3.
STOP RULE: no symptoms during, after, or next day. If holding the intake means cutting the route, cut the route. A day that returns 900m and a verified 80 g/h is a success; 900m at 30 g/h is a wasted last chance.
WHY IT IS THIS SIZE: cut from 195 to 130 on 24 Aug after the knee signal, and it is not restored without 10 consecutive symptom-free days including running. 29 Aug tested whether 80 g/h goes down at all; today tests whether it holds for four hours, which is the number that predicts hour six at Pirin.
